body: Forward test of the valuation-temperature method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.43 (naive base rate 0.48) that: Snowflake's share price return from 20-Nov-2026 to 30-Jun-2027 beats SPY's price return. Evidence: Yahoo monthly closes: SNOW $254.82 on 20-Nov-2026 (52-wk $118–385); SPY $689.81. SEC XBRL (10-Q): revenue $1.39bn (qtr to 30-Apr-2026) and $1.55bn (qtr to 31-Jul-2026, ≈$6.2bn run-rate); operating loss −$263m; SBC $402.5m in the April quarter vs FCF $232.8m; shares outstanding 352.5m (+1.7% QoQ) → market cap ≈$90bn ≈14–15× run-rate revenue, vs roughly 4× for CRM and ~3× for ADBE (our rough market-cap ÷ revenue); receivables +24% QoQ vs revenue +11%. Reasoning: Valuation-temperature test on a 'hot' growth name in a rising-rate tape (10-yr ~5%): long-duration, SBC-heavy equities are most rate-sensitive, and receivables outgrowing revenue is a small yellow flag. Q3 FY27 results due in early December add variance. We shade below the base. Resolution: YES if (SNOW close on 30-Jun-2027 ÷ 254.82) > (SPY close on 30-Jun-2027 ÷ 689.81). Use the last trading day ≤30-Jun-2027; adjust for splits; dividends ignored. Source: Yahoo Finance / NYSE closes (SNOW, SPY). Resolve by 2027-06-30; score with Brier vs base rate.

data.base_rate_reasoning: A single US large cap beats SPY over ~7 months a bit under half the time (~48%; skewed single-stock returns).
data.resolution_rule: YES if (SNOW close on 30-Jun-2027 ÷ 254.82) > (SPY close on 30-Jun-2027 ÷ 689.81). Use the last trading day ≤30-Jun-2027; adjust for splits; dividends ignored.

title: Paper call: Snowflake's share price return from 20-Nov-2026 to 30-Jun-2027 beats SPY's price return
